onboarding.welcome.title: Meet Jarvis
onboarding.welcome.body: A calm voice assistant that lives in your menu bar, answers out loud and hands real work to agents — asking before anything risky.
onboarding.mic.title: Jarvis needs your microphone
onboarding.mic.body: So you can talk instead of type. Jarvis only listens for its name until you speak to it.
onboarding.mic.promise: Nothing you say leaves this computer until you say “Jarvis”. You can mute it from the menu bar at any time.
onboarding.brain.title: Choose your brain
onboarding.brain.chatgpt.sub: Uses your Plus/Pro plan — no API key.
onboarding.brain.claude.sub: Uses your Claude subscription via Claude Code.
onboarding.brain.api.sub: Anthropic or OpenAI. Billed by usage. Stored in your system keychain.
onboarding.brain.local.sub: Ollama. Private, needs a capable computer.
onboarding.voice.title: Pick a voice
onboarding.try.title: Try it
settings.title: Settings
settings.name: Your name
settings.material.hint: Glass uses the system blur when available
settings.projects.empty: No projects yet. Say “Jarvis, create a project called shop in ~/Projects/shop”.
settings.muteDuringFocus: Pause during Focus / Do Not Disturb
settings.stt.cloud: Audio is sent only after a command is captured
settings.privateMode.hint: Speech, brain and voice all run on this computer. Nothing leaves it.
secret.hint: Stored in your system keychain, never on disk
models.title: On-device models
models.unavailable: Voice models are managed by the desktop app.
permission.label: Permission level for {project}
permission.confirm.title: Turn on Full auto for {project}?
permission.confirm.body: Agents will run commands, install packages and edit or delete files in this project without asking. High‑risk actions (deleting folders, pushing code, spending money) still show a card.
shortcut.pushToTalk.hint: Hold to talk, release to send
integrations.claudeDesktop.hint: Lets Claude Desktop and Cowork hand tasks to Jarvis and hear its voice.
integrations.chatgpt.hint: Pair the ChatGPT app on your phone to talk to Jarvis from anywhere, through your own relay. Scan the code or type it in.
integrations.writeTools.hint: Off by default; high-risk actions always need a click here
about.text: Jarvis is a calm voice assistant for macOS, Windows and Linux. Inter and JetBrains Mono are used under the SIL Open Font License.
composer.micTitle: Click to talk · hold to talk while pressed
composer.recording: Listening… click the mic to stop
footer.micLocal: Local only — nothing leaves this computer
history.empty.title: No history yet
history.empty.body: Your past conversations will show up here, grouped by day.
integrations.cli.hint: Adds Jarvis as an MCP server so agents can speak progress and ask for approval.
memory.empty: Jarvis doesn’t remember anything yet. Try: “Jarvis, remember that I prefer short answers”.
memory.sub: What Jarvis remembers about you. Delete anything — you can undo for a few seconds.
memory.title: Memory
onboarding.brain.sub: Use subscriptions you already pay for. Connect several — one is primary.
onboarding.mic.promiseTitle: The wake word runs on your computer
onboarding.mic.works: Your microphone works — say something and watch the bars.
onboarding.voice.sub: You can change it later in Settings.
permission.help: Safe asks before every command or file change. Trusted lets agents edit files and run common commands on their own. Full auto skips almost every question — high‑risk actions still need you.
projects.empty.title: No projects yet
projects.empty.body: Add a folder so agents can work in it. Try: “Jarvis, in project shop add a footer”.
settings.accent.desc: Drives the orb, focus rings and highlights.
settings.clearMemory.desc: Jarvis forgets everything it learned about you.
settings.defaultAgent.desc: Used when you don’t name one.
settings.material.desc: Glass lets your wallpaper through. Solid is opaque and easier to read.
settings.noPaidFallback: Never fall back to paid API
settings.noPaidFallback.desc: When a plan hits its cap, Jarvis stops and tells you instead.
settings.privateMode.note: Uses Ollama + Piper. Answers may be slower.
settings.speakReplies.desc: Off means Jarvis only shows text.
settings.theme.desc: Dark is the default. System follows your OS.
settings.wakeOnClap.desc: Experimental. Works best in a quiet room.
settings.wakeWord.desc: “Jarvis” is detected on this computer — audio isn’t sent anywhere until you’re heard.
integrations.install.hint: Downloads jarvis.mcpb. Open the downloaded file and Claude Desktop installs the extension (Cowork uses it too).
voice.hint.system: Uses your operating system’s default voice. Nothing to set up.
voice.hint.elevenlabs: Needs your ElevenLabs API key (below). Eleven v3 understands expressive tags such as [happy] or [whisper], which Jarvis adds on its own.
voice.hint.fish: Needs your Fish Audio API key (below). Fish also understands expressive tags, which Jarvis adds on its own.
voice.hint.openai: Needs an OpenAI API key (Brain & accounts › OpenAI API). The ChatGPT plan does not include voice.
voice.hint.kokoro: Runs on this computer. The voice model downloads the first time you press Preview.
voice.hint.piper: Runs on this computer. The voice downloads the first time you press Preview.
history.deleteHint: History can’t be deleted from here. To delete today’s history or everything, go to Settings › Privacy › Danger zone.
memory.howto: You can also just say: “Jarvis, remember that I prefer short answers”.
projects.sub: Folders your coding agents may work in. New projects start in Safe mode.
projects.name: Name
projects.add.hint: Say “Jarvis, in project <name> …” to use it. You can change its permissions with Permissions.
projects.remove.hint: Removes the project from Jarvis. The folder and its files are not touched.
voice.stability.hint: Lower = more expressive and varied, higher = steadier and more predictable.
voice.similarity.hint: How closely the voice sticks to the original recording.
voice.style.hint: Amplifies the voice’s style. Keep it low for the most stable result.
voice.speakerBoost.hint: Boosts similarity to the original speaker; slightly slower to generate.
settings.wakeByRecognition.desc: Better for Italian accents and other pronunciations. Short phrases are transcribed on this computer, and anything that does not start with “Jarvis” is discarded. Uses more CPU.
settings.echoCancellation.desc: Not available yet. Meanwhile Jarvis ignores what sounds like its own voice; headphones work best.
